summary: Outer range light at Port Dalhousie, St. Catharines: a square wooden tower of the late 1870s, still active at the end of the east pier, with a rear range tower that burned in 1898.

structures.type: square wooden tower at the end of the east pier
structures.note: LighthouseFriends gives 1878; the Canadian register gives the 1870s to 1880s

structures.type: octagonal wooden tower on the shore
structures.note: Built by William H. Noble after the 1898 fire; LighthouseFriends gives no year, and the register gives a distance of 300 ft from the front light

access.note: Grounds open; tower closed. Parking available near the pier.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (outer light); City of St. Catharines (inner tower, since 1997)

events.note: a light marks the harbour; funds for nails and wicking provided
severe gale destroys the lighthouse and injures most of the east pier; a frame lighthouse is hastily built
circular wooden lighthouse, 44 ft, on the capped east pier
a circular-burner lamp exploded and caused a fire; new iron lantern and new revolving apparatus installed
square wooden front range tower at the end of a new pier
new tower built on a new foundation after the old one was found too far gone; old lantern and apparatus reused, $2,157.51
inner (back range) lighthouse struck by lightning at 8:05 a.m. on 12 August and burned
the back range light changed from fixed red to occulting white on 1 June 1901 (Department report). LighthouseFriends gives 1 June 1902, when the range lights were electrified.
diaphone fog alarm in the front range lighthouse at the outer end of the east pier; one 4 s blast every 30 s
oil engine replaces the fog alarm's electric plant
inner light deactivated after the close of the 1988 navigation season
inner (discontinued) lighthouse designated a Recognized Federal Heritage Building, per LighthouseFriends
inner lighthouse transferred to the City of St. Catharines
inner lighthouse restored between 2000 and 2002; Coast Guard metal siding removed

notes_for_editor: 1) Front light build year: LighthouseFriends gives 1878; the Canadian register gives the 1870s to 1880s; the record gives 1879. No source read settles it. Brock University's Port Dalhousie exhibit pages, which the search results showed as a source for 1879, returned HTTP 403 to the reader, so they were not read or cited. 2) Distance between the towers: LighthouseFriends says the new rear tower stood 1,500 ft from the outer light; the register says 300 ft. The story gives both. 3) Light change: the Department's 1902 volume (scan 67) gives 1 June 1901 for the change from fixed red to occulting white at the back range tower; LighthouseFriends gives 1 June 1902. The story gives both. 4) Ownership of the inner tower: LighthouseFriends' text says it went to the City of St. Catharines in 1997; the LighthouseFriends rear page's owner line says Village of St. Catharines. The story follows the text. 5) Designation: the record gives a 1989 federal heritage building designation; LighthouseFriends gives 1990 for the inner tower; the register page read here gives no date. 6) The 1903 keeper list pairs 'Hunter, David' with Port Dalhousie. Checked on the page image (scan p. 235, printed p. 58) on 2026-10-27: the name and the station sit on one printed row. The same pairing also appears on one OCR line in the 1905-06 and 1906-07 reports. The pairing matches LighthouseFriends. 7) Record alias 'Port Dalhousie West Pier' conflicts with the east pier in LighthouseFriends and the register (see corrections). 8) Imperial-to-metric conversions in the story (1,245 ft, 300 ft, 1,500 ft, 44 ft) are ours. 9) Rear tower year of construction (after the 1898 fire) is not given in any source read; no event year is recorded for it. 10) LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: paraphrased; short quotations only in the evidence. 11) The 1901 volume (scan 50) is the Thirty-third Annual Report, for 1900; the story calls it 'the report for 1900' rather than dating the event to a calendar year. 12) The register (record 4743) gives the distance between the two towers as 300 ft; LighthouseFriends gives 1,500 ft for the new rear tower's planned site. The story states both and says the sources disagree.
